cells.tense: You are ending what is finished and letting the next thing come.
cells.ask: Name one thing you are carrying that already ran its course, and put it down today where someone can see you do it.
cells.core:
Something has ended and you are not fighting it. You let the finished thing finish and kept moving toward what is next, and that is not a small thing. You read what is over and you act on it, and the momentum stays clean because nothing is being propped up. Endings get taken on purpose here, and direction gets held through them.

The risk is not chaos. It is drift with a clear conscience — moving steadily without checking whether the motion still points where you wanted. So use one plain check: notice what you are holding, name what is finished, and set it down deliberately. What you feed forward matters more than how fast you go.
cells.sheetLine: You let what is over be over, and you keep moving.
cells.verb: ending what has run its course
cells.place: the place of steady forward motion through resistance

cells.tense: You will keep ending things before they have had a chance to be anything.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you were about to end and give it one more week of your full direction before you decide.
cells.core:
You are moving so hard toward what comes next that you keep cutting ties ahead of time. Somewhere ahead there is a version where everything is new and nothing drags, and you are living there — so anything that slows you looks like something to end, even if it has not started yet. The endings feel like freedom. A lot of them are fear that has learned to talk in those words.

Real direction does not need to destroy the ground behind it. Stay in contact with the people who are in this with you, without merging, without cutting them loose to protect your speed. What you are actually driving toward is clearer when you are not running from what is here.

cells.tense: You stood at a door that closed behind you and you are still there.
cells.ask: Let one honest feeling move you to one small action today — a call, a step, a start — and count only the movement.
cells.core:
You are still holding something that is over, and you are loyal to it. The direction went quiet in you — not because you cannot move, but because moving would mean admitting what ended. So you stay pointed at the closed door. Done well, this is simple: a person feels what has finished, lets it go, and walks toward the next thing without needing to know what it is.

What wakes this is not pushing at the empty motion. It is letting one real feeling decide one small act: not what duty asks, what you actually want to move toward once you stop defending the old thing. That is enough. The current comes back through the channel that is still warm.
cells.sheetLine: You are still holding what already ended, and calling it loyalty.

cells.tense: Something in you is already ending and you have not named it yet.
cells.ask: Write down one thing that has quietly stopped working, and set up one simple structure around it — a date, a rule, a way it ends.
cells.core:
You are already moving away from something. Not dramatically — no announcement, no decision — but the direction has shifted and you have not said so. You could describe the situation as simply being like this, as though it carried on without your hand in it. The turning is underway, and you have not put your name on it.

What this needs is structure, not more feeling. Give the ending a shape: a step, a date, something simple and reliable that organizes what is already happening. When you name it and put a container around it, the momentum you already have becomes yours again. That is what turns a drift into a direction you chose.
cells.sheetLine: You are already ending something. You just have not said so.
